briefings.title: From Restoring Sight to Reimagining the Brain, with Max Hodak
briefings.channel: No Priors: AI, Machine Learning, Tech, & Startups
briefings.tldr: Max Hodak, co-founder and CEO of Science Corporation, discusses the company's mission to treat the brain as a computational system—highlighting the commercial approval of their PRIMA retinal implant in Europe and their long-term vision of achieving substrate independence.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Max Hodak, co-founder and CEO of Science Corporation, discusses the company's mission to treat the brain as a computational system—highlighting the commercial approval of their PRIMA retinal implant in Europe and their long-term vision of achieving substrate independence. Sarah Guo hosts the discussion, exploring how bridging neuroscience with AI representations can revolutionize medicine and reduce the fragility of the human condition.

## Science Corporation & the PRIMA Retinal Implant
* **Company Mission:** Science Corporation is a medical device company focused on using a differentiated understanding of the brain to drive large effect sizes in medicine.
* **The PRIMA Product:** 
  * A tiny chip implanted under the retina in the back of the eye for patients blinded by the loss of light-sensitive cells (such as macular degeneration, retinitis pigmentosa, and Stargardt's disease).
  * Patients wear glasses equipped with a laser projector that projects an image onto the implant, stimulating the retina directly to bypass dead rods and cones and send visual signals to the brain.
* **Regulatory Milestone:** In July (2 years post-acquisition of the French company Pixium), Science received CE designation marketing approval in Europe to commercially sell PRIMA, with first sales scheduled for the coming weeks.
* **Clinical Results:** Clinical trials demonstrated patients filling in Sudoku/crossword puzzles and reading books, providing proof-of-concept for restoring form vision.

## The Brain as a Computer & BCI Taxonomy
* **Computational Framework:** Hodak views the brain and the universe literally as computers, arguing that matter can be arranged to solve computational problems over time.
* **BCI Landscape & Spectrum:** 
  * BCI is a broad category akin to "pharma," containing vastly different hypotheses and product types rather than a single bet.
  * **Low-impact/High-volume:** Products like silent speech or "brain keyboards" (speech-to-text, inner monologue capture) act primarily as hand substitutes or input devices, though humans may already be bottlenecked by language and cognitive limits (~10 bits per second).
  * **High-impact/Deep integration:** Restoring sensory modalities (vision, hearing, balance, motor control) redraws the border around the brain and moves toward the "Matrix" level of intervention.

## Science's Pipeline & Three-Pronged Strategy
* **Core Pipeline Elements:**
  1. **Vision:** Retinal prostheses and in-house gene therapies (next-gen going to human trials next year).
  2. **Biohybrid Neural Interfaces:** Research involving engrafting living neurons that grow in and form new biological connections.
  3. **Perfusion Medicine (Vessel Program):** A program targeting other medical areas like organ perfusion.
* **Targeting Major Killers:** Hodak argues that support organs (heart, pancreas, liver, lungs) exist to keep brain activity going, and believes perfusion and BCI programs will target major causes of death like cardiovascular disease and brain-metastasized cancer.

## AI Models and Neuroscience Parallels
* **Platonic Representation Hypothesis:** Internal mathematical objects and concept representations inside large AI models exhibit geometries very similar to those found in neuroscience.
* **Practical Alignment:** Science uses these parallels constructively to achieve alignments between animal brain neural recordings and AI model internal representations, signaling that AI is capturing true underlying data manifolds of intelligence.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Gene Therapy Trials:** Science's indigenously developed state-of-the-art gene therapy will go to human clinical trials next year (stated by Max Hodak).
* **Next-Gen Retinal Prosthesis:** The next version of the PRIMA retinal prosthesis is currently in animal studies and is targeted for human trials next year, expanding the addressable patient population from hundreds of thousands to millions (stated by Max Hodak).

## Notable Quotes
> *"Fundamentally, we're a medical device company. Um but I think if like the mission of lowercase S Science is to use a differentiated understanding of the universe to improve the human condition. I mean, that's that's the mission of uppercase S Science, that's what we do. We use uh specifically an understanding of how to work with the brain to get big effect sizes that you don't get in medicine often."* — **Max Hodak**

> *"The brain very literally, very clearly, plainly as a computer. You can solve computational problems by arranging matter in a certain way and then like taking your hands off and pressing go."* — **Max Hodak**

> *"If you can get the visual signal, auditory signal, balance, motor in and out of the brain, that is an end in itself, that is the central object."* — **Max Hodak**

briefings.title: Going In Deep On Data | YC Paper Club
briefings.tldr: Data quality, expert supervision, and data mixing have overtaken model architecture as the primary bottlenecks in AI development, generating over $100 billion in market capitalization and enabling new paradigms in real-time diffusion models and multilingual pre-training.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Data quality, expert supervision, and data mixing have overtaken model architecture as the primary bottlenecks in AI development, generating over $100 billion in market capitalization and enabling new paradigms in real-time diffusion models and multilingual pre-training.

## The Paradigm Shift to Data-Centric AI
* **The Evolution of AI Bottlenecks:** AI development has shifted from spending 95% of time on model architecture to spending over 97% of time on data curation, debugging, and environment design.
* **Focal Systems Lessons:** Interview questions at Focal Systems demonstrated that addressing production failures (such as store fridges covered in fog or blocked by customers) requires analyzing false positives and false negatives in the data rather than tweaking model layers or using alternative activation functions like ReLU versus GeLU.
* **Data as Software (Data 1.0):** Pioneered by Snorkel, "data programming" encodes expert supervision into labeling functions (heuristics) that can be refactored, audited, and processed via unsupervised label models to handle noisy data without manual labeling bottlenecks.

## Scaling Expert Supervision for Complex Agents (Data 2.0)
* **Senior SWE-Bench:** Developed in collaboration with the Princeton SWE-bench team to evaluate coding agents at a senior and principal engineering level using realistic natural language inputs (e.g., Slack messages and log dumps) rather than over-specified unit tests.
* **Validation Agent Architecture:** Combines high reliability and high flexibility by having human experts write a high-level validation spec (user stories), which a validation agent then translates into deterministic test scripts executed against the code patch.
* **"Tasteful Pass" Metric:** A new benchmark metric that measures not just code correctness and mergeability, but also whether an agent's code aligns with codebase practices, minimizes bloat, and exhibits senior-level software engineering judgment.
* **Benchmark Results:** Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus, and GPT-4o tied for first place on the Senior SWE-Bench leaderboard.

## Real-Time Diffusion Language Models
* **Mechanism of Diffusion Language Models:** Developed by Inception Labs (Mercury models), these models generate all tokens in parallel over multiple refinement steps rather than sequentially left-to-right.
* **Speed and Performance:** Mercury 2 achieves speeds exceeding 1,000 tokens per second on standard GPUs (rivaling specialized chips like Cerebras) while establishing a new Pareto frontier for quality and latency in real-time voice and latency-sensitive tasks.
* **Dow Forge Synthetic Environments:** An agentic harness used to synthesize realistic RL environments, policies, databases, and tasks based on real-world production logs and crawled business knowledge graphs to train and evaluate voice and workflow agents.
* **Training Impact:** Training Mercury 2.5 on tasks synthesized via Dow Forge improved downstream task accuracy by over 23%, matching state-of-the-art open-source and closed-source models.

## Multilingual Pre-Training and Data Mixing Laws
* **The Multilingual Data Constraint:** Low-resource languages like Thai (80 million speakers) have less than 0.6% of the token volume of English in common crawl datasets (e.g., Madlad 400), causing severe overfitting when trained in isolation.
* **Cross-Lingual Transfer Matrices:** Empirical measurement of language synergies and interference shows that training on auxiliary languages (e.g., Indonesian or Portuguese for Spanish) can significantly boost learning efficiency, though transfer is asymmetric and script/tokenization overlap heavily influences synergy.
* **Multilingual Scaling Laws:** A composite scaling law model adapts Chinchilla-style loss prediction to account for multi-source data mixtures, epoch repetition penalties, and diminishing returns across language families.

## Notable Quotes
> "If your answer was, oh, I would go read some papers... like add more layers... No. No. No. No. No. And the reason why is because you have to look at the data."
> — **Francois Chaubard**

> "We're already using coding agents like software engineers. We're vibe coding. We're trusting them to make architectural decisions... but we don't have good ways to evaluate them."
> — **Vincent Sunn Chen**

> "If you can make LLMs go much faster, if they can go at 1,000 tokens per second like our Mercury 2 models are able to achieve, then you can make real-time voice interactions feel more seamless."
> — **Volo Kuleshov**

briefings.title: How Borderless Founders Build Global Companies
briefings.tldr: Borderless founders—entrepreneurs who combine the local insights and networks of their home markets with the speed, talent, and capital of Silicon Valley—are increasingly building the next generation of global companies, accelerated by AI and powerful international diaspora networks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Borderless founders—entrepreneurs who combine the local insights and networks of their home markets with the speed, talent, and capital of Silicon Valley—are increasingly building the next generation of global companies, accelerated by AI and powerful international diaspora networks.

## The Origins and Evolution of International Investing at a16z
* **Initial Focus on Latin America:** 
  * Angela Strange and Gabriel Vasquez trace a16z's international investing back to early fintech investments in Latin America, starting with a check into Santiago Suarez (CEO of **Audi**, which now serves a quarter of the Colombian population).
  * The strategy originated from a WhatsApp group created by Vasquez, which brought together unicorn founders from Brazil, Colombia, and Mexico who were not previously connected, leading to shared deal flow and angel investments.
* **The AI Acceleration:** 
  * The rise of AI shifted the dynamic from a16z traveling to local regions (Brazil, Colombia) to founders actively wanting to integrate into the Bay Area faster.
  * While AI democratizes the ability to build from anywhere, it simultaneously concentrates the fastest-moving epicenter in the Bay Area.
* **The "Borderless Dinners" and Diaspora Networks:** 
  * a16z organized dinners mapping out successful founders from Latin America (such as Guillermo Rauch from **Vercel** and Pedro Franceschi from **Brex**) to mentor newcomers.
  * Early attendees of these groups (e.g., Victor Cardenas from **Slash**, Oreos from **Factories**) have now graduated into unicorn founders and speakers themselves.
  * International diasporas function similarly to powerful college alumni networks, driven by a deep desire to pay it forward to the next generation of founders.

## Defining the Borderless Founder
* **Inclusive Definition:** Anyone trying to build a global company internationally, whether they start building primarily in their home market or land directly in the US with global ambitions.
* **The "Chip on the Shoulder" Mindset:** 
  * Borderless founders often come from overlooked countries (e.g., Gabriel Vasquez growing up in El Salvador) or small rural towns, driving a desire to prove they can achieve greatness regardless of birthplace.
  * They contrast with traditional US founders who rely on "everything as a service" at every stack layer (e.g., fraud-as-a-stack, KYC-as-a-stack); international founders in regions like Latin America often have to build entire infrastructure stacks locally.
* **Geographic Expansion:** Beyond Latin America, a16z spends significant time in the UK, Sweden, Israel, and Germany.

## Native Advantages of Borderless Founders
* **Talent & Diaspora Networks:**
  * Borderless founders map top engineering and business talent from their home countries living in Silicon Valley.
  * Companies like **Taco** in Brazil are actively recruiting Brazilian talent back from the US to solve local bureaucratic challenges using AI.
  * Founders leverage non-obvious talent pools, such as regional scholarship programs and robotics competitions, rather than just top-tier university brands.
* **Brand & Government Validation:**
  * Polish founders of **11 Labs** became national representatives in the "AI Olympics," securing direct investment and initiatives from the Polish government.
  * Swedish government support gave early-stage validation to startups like **Lovable** and **Gora**, opening doors to large enterprises.
  * A strong local brand acts as a beacon to attract top international talent back to home markets (e.g., recruiting credit experts from Capital One to move to Bogota for **Audi**).
* **Customer Base & Design Partnerships:**
  * Early design partnerships with major conglomerates (e.g., **Factor Labs** working with the Slim family's conglomerate in Latin America) convert into multi-million dollar contracts and expand into broader enterprise workflows.
  * Conversely, top Silicon Valley AI companies like **Cognition** found early go-to-market traction and high revenue shares by selling into hungry enterprise markets in Brazil.

## Ecosystem Building, Repeat Founders, and Silicon Valley Integration
* **Ecosystem Playbooks & Local Luminaries:**
  * a16z identifies "local luminaries"—respected local operators (e.g., Fredrik Hjelm of **Voi** in Sweden) who angel-invest and connect younger builders to the global stage.
  * Global scout programs recruit rising stars at international companies to foster local density.
* **Repeat Founders:**
  * First-generation unicorn founders who achieved $1B–$5B outcomes are returning with deeper lessons to build even larger companies (e.g., Fredrik Hjelm's new company, **pip.com**).
  * These repeat founders provide elite "CEO school" experience for young, ambitious engineers working under them for a few years.
* **Tactical Soft-Landing Support:**
  * **Visas:** a16z helps founders navigate the stressful US visa process, including investing in native visa platforms like **Extraordinary**.
  * **Hacker Houses & Campuses:** a16z sponsored **Palo House** (originated by students from Germany's CDTM program met at Slush in Finland), which hosted 1,200 people over 4 months, acting as a mini-college liberal arts incubator for international tech talent.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Global Venture Returns Share (Gabriel Vasquez):** The share of venture capital returns coming from Silicon Valley companies will shift from roughly 10% toward 20% to 30%, bolstered by global borderless companies with dual-country footprints (headquarters in the US, engineering in home markets).
* **Continued Growth of International Investing (Angela Strange):** International investing trends will continue to scale; out of recent a16z apps, 40% of investments were in international founders (split evenly between US-based and foreign-based).

## Notable Quotes
> "You could compete to be the fifth financial services for every customer in the US. Or you could go to a wide open market with five fat, happy banks that only serve 20% of the population."
> — **Angela Strange** *(recounting advice heard regarding Nubank and Latin America)*

> "Unlike in the US where you can get everything as a service at every layer of the stack... in many other markets, you just can't do that. There's no fraud-as-a-stack, KYC-as-a-stack; so you end up having to build everything."
> — **Angela Strange**

> "Every country wants to have their own candidates winning medals... so like for Poland, 11 Labs has become that candidate."
> — **Gabriel Vasquez**

> "In every country I make them feel like it's the only country that I look at."
> — **Gabriel Vasquez** *(describing his deep, localized approach to international ecosystems)*

briefings.title: Race to Save Humanity: Inside $12B Colossal Biosciences & $3.8B Astromech
briefings.tldr: Colossal Biosciences is a $12 billion de-extinction and genome engineering company using AI and reproductive technologies to revive extinct species, having raised $635 million total—including an oversubscribed $400 million round.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Colossal Biosciences is a $12 billion de-extinction and genome engineering company using AI and reproductive technologies to revive extinct species, having raised $635 million total—including an oversubscribed $400 million round. Alongside its AI biology spinout Astromech (valued at $3.8 billion), the company aims to apply its biotechnology stack to solve global challenges in invasive species, conservation, and human healthcare.

## Company Metrics & Funding History
* **Capital Raised:** **$635 million** total funding to date, featuring a recent **$400 million** round that was originally targeted at **$200 million** and heavily oversubscribed (Ben Lamm).
* **Valuation & Standing:** Colossal is valued at **$12 billion** and is described by Co-founder and CEO Ben Lamm as "one of the most undervalued companies in the world."
* **Spinout Metrics:** **Astromech**, Colossal's AI biology spinout co-founded with George Church, recently raised **$20 million** at a **$3.8 billion** valuation.
* **Team & Network:** **260+** internal employees, **17** academic partners, **80** researchers funded in external academic labs, and **95** advisors across scientific, indigenous, executive, and youth advisory boards (Ben Lamm).

## Technology Stack & Vertical Integration
* **First-Principles Infrastructure:** Built completely under one roof across a 55,000-square-foot headquarters and 30,000 square feet of lab space to ensure vertical integration across the entire biological pipeline (Ben Lamm).
* **Multiplex Editing Records:** Produced second-generation "woolly mice"—the second most genetically modified multicellular organisms after direwolves—engineered using 100% healthy cells, predicted phenotypes, and the largest multiplex edits ever delivered simultaneously, completed in **30 days** (Ben Lamm).
* **Hardware & Automation:** Innovated custom hardware, screen-capture computer vision systems, and automated embryology setups (including specialized laser positioning and nuclear transfer tools) to streamline cloning and cellular extraction (Ben Lamm).
* **Vioagen Acquisition:** Bolstered biobanking and cloning capabilities by acquiring Vioagen, achieving cloning efficiencies of **80%** compared to the industry standard of **2%** (Ben Lamm).

## Business Model & Commercial Applications
* **Civilization Tech & Secondary Markets:** Beyond de-extinction, the company develops fundamental biotechnology platforms with massive commercial applications:
  * **Invasive Species & Biocontrol:** Utilizing gene drives to combat multi-billion-dollar problems like the screwworm in Texas (which threatens beef prices and cattle) and tick-borne Lyme disease, potentially eradicating specific populations in **6 to 7 months** compared to traditional multi-year tax-funded programs (Ben Lamm).
  * **Human Healthcare & Drug Discovery:** Astromech applies AI to evolutionary trends (such as cancer-suppressing p-53 gene expressions in elephants) to build predictive drug and therapeutic models for human health, bird flu, and disease resistance (Ben Lamm).
  * **Ethical Manufacturing & Supply Chain Solutions:** Developing lab-grown biological alternatives—such as elephant stem-cell-derived hair follicles grown on plates to produce mammoth hair equivalents—to service industrial partners facing raw material shortages (Ben Lamm).
* **Conservation Strategy & Open Source:** Open-sourcing all proprietary technologies for free to the global conservation community, resulting in a measurable increase in funding and awareness for partner organizations (Ben Lamm).

## Brand, Culture, & Public Engagement
* **"Harvard Meets MTV":** Explicitly designed to merge rigorous academic science with pop-culture accessibility, utilizing cinematic office architecture, custom apparel, and digital-first communication strategies targeting the next generation (Ben Lamm).
* **Conspiracy & Public Demands:** Regularly receives widespread public inquiries, bootleg merchandise requests, and viral internet theories regarding extinct species (such as woolly mice and direwolves) and fictional creatures like Megalodons (Ben Lamm).

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Digital Twin of Nature:** Ben Lamm predicts that humanity will converge AI and biological data to "build a digital twin of nature" within the future, providing real-time prediction models for ecosystems similar to missile defense or seismic systems.
* **Extinct Species Birth Timeline:** Ben Lamm targets the next **12 months** for Colossal to potentially have its next birthed extinct species.
* **Editing Capacity Milestones:** Ben Lamm claims the company is pushing a new delivery mechanism designed to execute **thousands of edits at once**, scaling past current capabilities of hundreds of simultaneous edits.

## Notable Quotes
> "I think that Colossal is one of the most undervalued companies in the world... the ability to like preserve, engineer, and direct life on a planetary scale in all species I think is a pretty important skill set for humanity."
> — **Ben Lamm**

> "We are not an academic lab. We're not a think tank. We're not a biotech that's going to just work on one solution. We have to innovate across the entire spectrum of the pipeline."
> — **Ben Lamm**

> "If you spend time with that community and you ask them are we as a whole as humanity as a whole with current modern conservation techniques are we winning the fight to save species and they will all tell you no. So it's okay, we got to do something different."
> — **Ben Lamm**

briefings.title: Rackspace Technology at Palantir Sovereignty Bootcamp | August 2026
briefings.tldr: Rackspace became "Customer Zero" for sovereign AI by shifting ~70% of its back office to Palantir's Ontology, Foundry, and AIP—starting with a daily sales CRM—while partnering with Dell, NVIDIA, and Palantir to deploy and operate fully controlled sovereign cloud environments for enterprise customers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Rackspace became "Customer Zero" for sovereign AI by shifting ~70% of its back office to Palantir's Ontology, Foundry, and AIP—starting with a daily sales CRM—while partnering with Dell, NVIDIA, and Palantir to deploy and operate fully controlled sovereign cloud environments for enterprise customers.

## Strategic Pivot & "Customer Zero" Transformation
* **Company Evolution:** 
  * Rackspace is a 27-year-old company that evolved from the old days of cloud computing and managed infrastructure into an enterprise AI company.
  * Over the last 12 months under CEO Gajen Kandiah, the company needed to fundamentally change everything to accelerate growth and move at the speed of digital businesses.
* **Becoming Customer Zero:** 
  * Rackspace decided to become "Customer Zero" for Palantir to learn the technology firsthand, bring those lessons to customers as forward-deployed engineer (FDE) services, and run Palantir on a sovereign cloud.
  * The goal is to move about **70%** of Rackspace's back office onto Palantir, eliminating a ton of legacy tech while retaining necessary systems to handle 27 years of background data and SKUs-to-solutions business motions.
* **Starting with CRM:** 
  * Rackspace targeted its CRM as the initial entry point because it represents the most complex yet high-pace operational bottleneck, touching everything from initial customer contact to the back office and standing up GPUs. Billing was slated to come next.

## The "MCAT" Framework & Data Sovereignty
* **The MCAT Philosophy:** 
  * For sovereignty to be real, an organization must own four core pillars: **Model, Compute, Alpha, and Data** (dubbed "MCAT" by Kandiah).
* **Ontology as a Digital Twin:** 
  * Palantir Ontology acts as a digital twin of the business data, allowing Rackspace to run agents on top of it for real-time visibility rather than running the business using a rearview mirror.
* **Core Sovereignty Questions:** 
  * Rackspace's board subjected the initiative to rigorous tests to answer:
    * *Where does the data live, and can any government compel access to it?*
    * *What do we own across our AI environment versus what does someone else own?*
    * *Can we change models without losing intelligence?*
    * *Can we prove all of the above?*
* **Ring-Fencing Intelligence:** 
  * Although Rackspace uses tools like Anthropic and OpenAI, the company realized the model itself is not the asset—**what you teach the model is the asset** (alpha/intelligence). Ring-fencing data at the core point of access and defining roles directly within the data layer ensures complete sovereignty without data leaving the firewall.

## Sovereign Workloads & Infrastructure Partnerships
* **Categorizing Workloads:** 
  * Rackspace breaks workloads down into regulated, sovereign, and institutional sovereign tiers, recognizing they must run across on-premises, edge, core, and public cloud environments.
* **Sovereign Pods Partnership:** 
  * Through a partnership with **NVIDIA, Dell, and Palantir**, Rackspace is building and deploying single- or multi-tenant "sovereign pods" within the Rackspace environment.
* **Deploy and Operate Motion:** 
  * Kandiah emphasized that deploying alone is insufficient; companies must be able to run and operate sovereign environments continuously due to the iterative nature of the business.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **CEO Vision on Enterprise AI:** Gajen Kandiah noted a prediction made by a frontier model CEO that in the future there will be only two types of entities: that specific company and governments—underscoring the critical importance of organizations retaining control over their own intelligence and alpha.

## Notable Quotes
> *"We were a digital business with a very manual process, right? And we needed something to move at the speed at which the digital businesses were moving. So, we decided that we were going to become customer zero."* — Gajen Kandiah

> *"In my head, there's MCAT, right? So the model matters, the compute matters, the alpha matters and the data matters. Those four things and you need to own all of those for sovereignty to be real."* — Gajen Kandiah

> *"The model is not the asset. It's what we teach the model, that is the asset. Right? And that is what we define as, as intelligence."* — Gajen Kandiah
